name: Cerebrolysin
summary: A mixture of small peptides from pig brain, prescribed abroad for stroke and dementia and taken for focus and memory; not approved in the US, with weak supporting evidence.
what_it_is: Cerebrolysin is a mixture of small peptides and amino acids taken from pig brain tissue and made into an injectable solution. It is made by an Austrian company and prescribed there for dementia, stroke and brain injury, and it is widely used for stroke in Russia, Eastern Europe, China and other Asian countries. It is not approved in the US.

evidence.why: Several mostly industry-supported randomized trials exist: Cochrane rated the evidence for better thinking in vascular dementia very low certainty, and pooled stroke trials (7 trials, 1,773 people) found no reduction in deaths but more non-fatal serious adverse events.

status_us.label: Not approved in the US; prescription drug abroad
status_us.note: The manufacturer states that Cerebrolysin is not registered with FDA and is not approved for sale or distribution in the US. It has not been nominated for US pharmacy compounding.

benefits.claim: Better scores on memory and thinking tests and on overall clinical impression in people with vascular dementia, in 6 small industry-supported trials (597 people) that Cochrane rated very low certainty

risks.risk: More non-fatal serious adverse events than standard stroke care alone (about 2.4 times the risk, moderate-certainty evidence), although total serious adverse events and deaths did not differ

Overall side effects were similar to control groups in stroke trials (low-certainty evidence) and in the two dementia trials that could be pooled; the maker describes reported reactions as transient and mild

avoid_if: Epilepsy (a contraindication in the manufacturer's prescribing information)
Allergy to any of its components (a contraindication)

labs.why: No evidence-based monitoring exists; kidney function matters because the manufacturer lists severe kidney impairment as a contraindication.

studies.title: Cerebrolysin for acute ischaemic stroke
studies.people: 1,773 people with acute ischemic stroke in 7 randomized trials
studies.finding: Adding Cerebrolysin (or the similar Cortexin) to standard care probably does not reduce deaths and probably increases non-fatal serious adverse events. Three trials involved the manufacturer.

studies.title: Cerebrolysin for vascular dementia
studies.people: 597 people with vascular dementia in 6 randomized trials
studies.finding: Cerebrolysin courses improved cognition and global function, but the evidence was very low certainty, the trials had high risk of bias, and the reported funders were drug companies.

ask_your_clinician: What is causing my memory or focus problems, and which proven treatments fit?
Given that stroke trials found more serious side effects, is any benefit worth the risk for me?
Do I have epilepsy, kidney problems or another condition that rules it out?

sources.title: Bulk Drug Substances Nominated for Use in Compounding Under Section 503A of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (updated May 14, 2026)

notes_for_editor: No FDA document states Cerebrolysin's status directly; 'not approved in the US' comes from the manufacturer's own site (source 1), and FDA's lists (503A May 2026, 503B March 2025, Category 2 page) do not mention it. Contraindications come from the same page, which says its prescribing information is based on the Austrian SmPC; the full SmPC (side-effect frequencies, interactions) was not opened. The manufacturer page date is the access year. The 2023 Cochrane stroke review pooled one Cortexin trial with the Cerebrolysin trials; its background names pig brain, while its plain-language summary says cows and pigs. The benefit row for stroke deaths records a null result graded by the review's moderate certainty. Alzheimer's disease and traumatic brain injury trials were not reviewed within the search budget. WADA's 2026 list does not name Cerebrolysin.
